title: White jazz bands among Black bands; Strand and Orpheum stage
summary: White says few white jazz bands existed then, the Owls were college boys treating it as a lark, and recounts the Strand contest win and an Orpheum week.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: rub it out, but, that was a fact. And, uh, it was, because, uh, except for the fact, that most of us, had been, had even, had a year of college or so, and were, pretty well known in New Orleans, uh, you take, most of those boys, that were with us, were, from excellent families, and, didn't consider it a livelihood, they considered it, a lark, is what they did, but the thing got control, and it became a livelihood, with us, for quite a number of years. And then, well, to get back to the whole history, the Owls, after, after we, we played the, the Roosfelt, then we went to, uh, we, went to the, uh, well, we played, first of all, we played on the Strand Theater, as you know, we won that contest, and played on the Strand Theater, uh, for a week, then we, went to the Roosfelt, we left the Roosfelt, we didn't leave then, but we went on the, on the Orpheum, stage, for a week, I don't know how we got on there, frankly, I don't remember what the circumstances were, that got us on there,
